decision: User decisions 2026-09-16/17 (scripts/cloud/reports/variants-20260916/PLAN.md): predictor/judge ablations {flash_quality, mlp_quality, mlp_length} x {hard, score, latency_agnostic} x {7, 8, 8.3} QPS x 16,000 requests = 27 fresh Qwen cells (6 QPS dropped on 18 September 2026: the canonical grid shows little differentiation there). No-op policies are not rerun; their canonical cells are reused. Comparators: canonical hard and score from the Vast SFS/SCORE overlay (sfs-score-campaign-20260917.json); canonical latency_agnostic from the April Bridges reference (host/source difference accepted by the user; labelled provider=bridges). hard_prefill_tps is deferred. One pool per variant, each qualified separately (--variant is per pool).

variants.flash_quality: router --accuracy-model-path = bundle variants/flash_quality (LightGBM trained on Flash labels); servers byte-identical to canonical; primary judge at collation = Flash
variants.mlp_quality: router --accuracy-model-path = bundle variants/mlp_quality; servers byte-identical to canonical
variants.mlp_length: router and every Qwen server --output-length-model-path = bundle variants/mlp_length

hard.note: Canonical SFS rerun on Vast with the same rule-ON 0.6B engine; 8 QPS may be a reused lane control only if the user writes its ledger entry (see the SFS/SCORE overlay reuse note)

score.note: Canonical SCORE has no result at these rates anywhere; the Vast cells are both main-grid entries and the ablation comparator

latency_agnostic.note: April 2026 Bridges canonical latency_agnostic reference (current reserve rule, Bridges H100 hosts); the user accepted it as the comparator on 2026-09-17 in place of a Vast rerun. variant_matrix.json labels these rows provider=bridges with the point path and sha256; OnTimeUtility is recomputed from the point on the observed judge cohort when the point is readable.

remaining_length.note: The rule is per engine: only the qwen3-0.6b server receives --remaining-length-mode running_all --remaining-length-table qwen3-0.6b.json --remaining-length-quantile 0.5 --remaining-length-conditioning prompt_bin, and the router attaches that table for its missing-prediction fill on that instance only. qwen3-8b and qwen3-32b stay off: reserve-tail-20260916 README sections 4.2/4.3 (8B target component within noise, hindsight replay worse under every candidate; 32B sub-second either way). Ministral stays off: no Ministral paired evidence (reserve-tail-ministral-20260917 is analysis only), the rule is only plumbed for the Qwen family and scripts.cloud.pool refuses it for a Ministral server. Tables were built from the calibration outputs only (zero overlap with the 16,000 evaluation ids); manifest.json records the build paths on the controller. The rule applies to every Qwen SFS/SCORE run from now on and, because the engine flag is per pool, it is simply on for the 0.6B engine in every Qwen pool of this overlay: latency_agnostic reads no snapshots and its routing is unaffected by the engine-side targets, but its cells run on the same rule-ON pool and record remaining_length_rule = qwen3-0.6b=running_all_prompt_bin_q50 like the hard and score cells. The Bridges latency_agnostic comparator ran under the current rule on Bridges hardware (user-accepted difference).

evidence.paired_run: scripts/cloud/reports/reserve-tail-20260916/paired-qps8p6-on/result_summary.json (Vast /workspace/sfs/state/diagnostics/reserve-tail-20260916/paired-qps8p6-on; canonical 8.6 QPS hard control, 16,000 requests, source bedeec4 + reserve diff)
evidence.reading: ON exceeds the better OFF control on both acceptance metrics (attainment 90.89 vs 63.71 percent; Pro OnTimeUtility 0.4732 vs 0.3561), outside the 13.8-point OFF spread; the pre-registered reading rule in the readiness note therefore admits the 0.6B rule for the campaign.
